context.title: Seeking the Lost
context.summary: Zacchaeus, a rich tax collector, climbs a tree to see Jesus and is changed. Jesus tells the parable of the pounds, rides into Jerusalem, weeps over the city, and clears the temple.
context.background: Jericho was a wealthy town on a trade route, and Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector there. Many note that the parable's nobleman who travels to receive a kingdom recalls Archelaus, Herod's son, who went to Rome to be confirmed as ruler while a delegation opposed him.

customs.note: The law required a thief to repay four sheep for one stolen (Exodus 22:1). Zacchaeus applies that standard to himself.
A mina, worth about a hundred denarii, roughly a hundred days' wages.

watchFor: 'The Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost' (v. 10).
Jesus weeps over Jerusalem and foretells a siege (vv. 41–44).

people.name: Zacchaeus
people.summary: Pure, a superintendant of customs; a chief tax-gather (publicanus) at Jericho (Luke 19:1-10). “The collection of customs at Jericho, which at this time produced and exported a considerable quantity of balsam, was undoubtedly an important post, and would account for Zacchaeus being a rich man.”

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea.

places.name: Jericho
places.summary: Place of fragrance, a fenced city in the midst of a vast grove of palm trees, in the plain of Jordan, over against the place where that river was crossed by the Israelites (Josh. 3:16).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Bethany
places.summary: A village on the south-eastern slope of the Mount of Olives (Mark 11:1), about 2 miles east of Jerusalem, on the road to Jericho. It derived its name from the number of palm-trees which grew there.

places.name: Bethphage
places.summary: House of the unripe fig, a village on the Mount of Olives, on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho (Matt. 21:1; Mark 11:1; Luke 19:29), and very close to Bethany.

places.name: Olivet
places.summary: so called from the olive trees with which its sides are clothed, is a mountain ridge on the east of Jerusalem ( 1 Kings 11:7 ; Ezekiel 11:23 ; Zechariah 14:4 ), from which it is separated by the valley of Kidron.

places.name: mount of Olives
places.summary: So called from the olive trees with which its sides are clothed, is a mountain ridge on the east of Jerusalem (1 Kings 11:7; Ezek. 11:23; Zech. 14:4), from which it is separated by the valley of Kidron.

events.title: Zaccheus Converted and Parable of the Pounds
events.summary: Passage: Luke 19:1–28. People: Jesus, Zacchaeus. Place: Jericho.

events.title: Holy Week
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 21:1 – John 20:31. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 8 days.

events.title: Triumphal Entry
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 21:1 – John 12:19. People: Jesus. Place: Jerusalem.

events.title: Temple Cleansed
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 21:12 – Luke 19:48. People: Jesus. Place: Jerusalem.
